title.rendered: Enthusiastic Firing Training Conducted at CATC–I Camp

content.rendered:
As part of the Combined Annual Training Camp (CATC–I) being organized by the 23(A) Battalion NCC at St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology, Chirala, a firing training session was conducted on Wednesday. The training aimed to enhance the cadets’ shooting skills, which are an essential component of military training.

The firing practice was closely supervised by Camp Commandant Colonel Gopal Tripathi and Deputy Camp Commandant Lieutenant Colonel N.S. Parmar, who provided valuable guidance and instructions to both the staff and cadets. They emphasized that adherence to safety protocols, discipline, and accuracy in target shooting are vital qualities every cadet must develop.

Before the practical session, cadets were given detailed instructions on weapon handling, safety regulations, precautions during firing, aiming techniques, breathing control, and trigger control. Following the briefing, the cadets participated in a structured firing practice session at the firing range, where their skills and performance were assessed.

The training was conducted under the supervision of Subedar Major Ranveer Singh, Camp Adjutant Major Y. Anji Reddy, Training JCO Subedar Ravindra Singh, Associate NCC Officer Lieutenant Medikonda Rajesh Babu, BHM P. Ramesh, and Havildar Ramesh. Cadets participated with great enthusiasm and dedication.

Officials stated that cadets who demonstrated outstanding performance during the firing practice would be shortlisted to represent the 23rd Andhra Battalion in the Six-District Level Firing Selection Competitions scheduled to be held on June 19 and 21.

The officials further noted that firing training plays a crucial role in developing concentration, self-confidence, discipline, patience, and leadership qualities among cadets. They also informed that, as part of the camp, training programs on drill, map reading, field craft, personality development, and yoga are being conducted alongside other activities.

title.rendered: CATC–I NCC Training Camp Inaugurated at St. Ann’s College, Chirala

content.rendered:
The Combined Annual Training Camp–I (CATC–I), organized under the aegis of the 23 Andhra Pradesh Battalion NCC, was inaugurated with great enthusiasm today at St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology, Chirala. Addressing the cadets during the opening ceremony, Camp Commandant Colonel Gopal Tripathi emphasized the vital role of NCC in shaping disciplined, patriotic, and responsible young citizens.

He stated that NCC training significantly contributes to developing leadership qualities, self-confidence, discipline, and a spirit of service among cadets. He encouraged all participants to make the best use of the training opportunities provided during the camp and strive for excellence.

Highlighting the importance of the camp, Colonel Tripathi noted that it serves as a crucial platform for the selection of cadets for the prestigious Thal Sainik Camp (TSC). He described TSC as one of the most esteemed NCC events in the country and urged cadets to actively participate in activities such as drill, map reading, tent pitching, obstacle training, firing, and other competitive events to showcase their abilities.

He further advised cadets to approach competitions with true sportsmanship, focusing not merely on winning or losing but on learning, teamwork, mutual cooperation, and discipline. He encouraged every cadet to give their best performance, as outstanding participants would have the opportunity to advance to higher-level selections for the Thal Sainik Camp. He also explained how NCC training helps build leadership skills, confidence, and dedication towards national service.

On the occasion, Deputy Camp Commandant Lieutenant Colonel N. S. Parmar briefed the cadets about the camp schedule and training modules. He informed them that the camp would include training sessions on drill, weapon training, map reading, field craft, personality development, leadership, sports, and cultural activities.

The inaugural function was attended by Subedar Major Ranveer Singh, Camp Adjutant Major Y. Anji Reddy, Lieutenant Medikonda Rajesh Babu, First Officers P. Suresh Babu and T. Venkateswarlu, Second Officer G. Gopinath, Training JCO Ravindra Singh, and BHM P. Ramesh. A large number of NCC cadets from various educational institutions participated enthusiastically in the opening ceremony, making the event a grand success.

title.rendered: Guest Lecture on “Software Engineering Beyond the Classroom”

He further spoke about the opportunities in the field of Machine Learning and its applications across industries. Emphasizing industry requirements, he explained how choosing the right programming language based on project needs plays a crucial role in successful software development. He also guided students on how to grow in the software industry beyond classroom-based theoretical knowledge.

The session included an interactive segment where students’ queries were clarified in detail, as stated by the Head of the AI & ML Department, Dr. C. H. Harikrishan.

The guest lecture was coordinated by Dr. P. S. Naveen Kumar as the Convener. The program witnessed active participation from the Head of the AI & ML Department, faculty members, and a large number of students, making the event informative and successful.

The lecture provided valuable exposure to industry-oriented knowledge and practical insights, greatly benefiting the students’ professional development.

title.rendered: ATAL Online FDP Inaugurated at St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology, Chirala

content.rendered:
St. Ann’s College of Engineering and Technology, Chirala, has inaugurated the AICTE–ATAL Online Faculty Development Program (FDP) being conducted from 10th November 2025 to 15th November 2025.

Program Overview

The six-day online FDP is organized under the guidance of the AICTE Training and Learning (ATAL) Academy.
College Secretary Sri Vanama Ramakrishna Rao and Correspondent Sri Y. Lakshmana Rao officially announced the commencement of the program.
Principal Dr. K. Jagadeesh Babu highlighted that the FDP focuses on strengthening faculty knowledge in cutting-edge areas of Cyber Security and Digital Forensics.

Key Focus Areas

The FDP will cover advanced topics including:

  • Forensic Cyber Security
  • Concept Research, Trends & Processes
  • Policy & Compliance
  • Cyber Crime & Investigation
  • Digital Forensics
  • Forensic Tools & Techniques
  • Malware Analysis
  • Blockchain & Digital Identity
  • Cyber Laws & Legal Framework
  • Research Directions & Case Studies

Experts from IITs, NITs, academia, and industry will deliver sessions throughout the program.

Program Conveners

  • Dr. Indraneel Sriram – Professor & Head, Department of IoT (Convener)
  • Dr. V. V. Praveen Kumar – Associate Professor (Co-Convener)

Inaugural Session

The online inauguration witnessed participation from:

  • Dr. C. Subba Rao – Director, Accreditations
  • Faculty members from various institutions across the country

The program aims to enhance faculty expertise in the rapidly evolving domain of cyber security and forensic technologies.

title.rendered: First Year B.Tech Induction Programme Concludes Successfully at St. Ann’s College, Chirala

content.rendered:
St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology, Chirala conducted a grand Induction Programme on August 4, 2025, for newly admitted First Year B.Tech students. The event was held to welcome and orient the freshers, and it was formally announced by College Secretary Sri Vanama Ramakrishna Rao and Correspondent Sri Y.S. Lakshmana Rao in a joint press statement.

The programme was graced by Dr. K.V.S.G. Murali Krishna, Former Vice-Chancellor of JNTU Kakinada, as the Chief Guest. He appreciated the college for achieving 100% admissions and encouraged the management to continue delivering quality education with futuristic teaching methods and to prepare responsible citizens for the nation.

📌 Key Highlights from the Induction Programme:

🏫 Principal’s Address:

College Principal Dr. K. Jagadeesh Babu emphasized that choosing St. Ann’s for pursuing B.Tech is a wise decision. With a committed teaching faculty and state-of-the-art infrastructure, the college provides an excellent platform for students’ futures. He shared details about:

  • The college’s prestigious accreditations
  • Extensive placement opportunities
  • Faculty strength of 250+, including 50+ Ph.D. holders
  • Appointment of counselors for every 20 students to guide progress
  • Regular parent-faculty interactions every 15 days
  • Mobile phone and private vehicle restrictions
  • Dual degree options for non-CSE students to boost career prospects

🛠 Vision by the Founders:

  • Founder Chairman Vanama Venkateswara Rao, Former Minister, recalled the college’s humble beginnings in 2001 with 180 students and its remarkable growth to 6,000+ students today. He expressed the vision of seeing 10,000 students learning at the college in the near future.
  • Chairman Vanama Raghavendra Rao aspired for students to bring global recognition to the institution by achieving placements in top domestic and international companies.
  • Vice Chairman B. Phani Raju mentioned that the college ensures convenient transport facilities so that students can commute safely to and from campus each day. He encouraged students to stay focused and aim high.

🗣 Chief Guest’s Message – Dr. K.V.S.G. Murali Krishna:

Dr. Murali Krishna motivated students to:

  • Develop self-confidence and focus on learning
  • Practice what they learn
  • Set long-term goals and work with consistency, discipline, and hard work
  • Cultivate reading habits and make books their best friends
  • Show respect for elders, stay humble, and grow with purpose
    He also shared success stories of university alumni and stressed that students’ futures are shaped by their daily efforts and positive attitude.

🏅 Student Recognitions:

  • Academic toppers from 2024–25 were honored with mementos
  • Sheik Farzana was felicitated for receiving the University Gold Medal
  • Mohammad Khaja Vali was honored for winning Gold Medals in National & International Weightlifting and Powerlifting Competitions

🙏 Special Felicitations:

  • Dr. K.V.S.G. Murali Krishna was felicitated by the management
  • College committee members including A. Umamaheswara Rao, Paritala Satyanarayana, Dr. C. Subbarao (Director – R&D & Accreditations), and R.V. Ramana Murthy (Administrative Manager) were also present
  • The program was convened by Mr. Y.S. Amarnath, In-charge of First Year B.Tech, who explained the student monitoring system and induction policies

At the end of the programme, dignitaries on the stage released doves symbolizing peace and prosperity.

title.rendered: International Women’s Day Celebrations – March 8, 2025 (Saturday)

content.rendered:
St. Ann’s College of Engineering and Technology, Chirala, celebrated International Women’s Day with grandeur on March 8, 2025, under the auspices of the college’s Women Empowerment Cell. The event was jointly announced by the College Secretary Vanama Ramakrishna Rao and Correspondent Y.S. Lakshman Rao in a statement.

Anita from Anita Hospital, Chirala, as informed by the Principal of the college, Dr. K. Jagadish Babu. On this occasion, the Principal expressed his wish for women to use the opportunities available in education, employment, and the industrial sector without gender discrimination, and to achieve high status and recognition in modern society. He emphasized that women today play a crucial role in all sectors and encouraged everyone to work towards women’s empowerment.

Dr. Anita, the Chief Guest, highlighted the growing mental health issues among modern women, such as depression, PCOD, obesity, high blood pressure, and joint pains. She mentioned that personal and professional challenges are leading to mental struggles for women. She urged women to pay attention to their health, adopt a healthy diet, and maintain both physical and mental well-being. She also emphasized the importance of making wise decisions on financial and family matters and urged women to serve as role models for future generations.

Y.S.K. Rihana, Principal Junior Civil Judge, shared that inspiration is crucial in students’ lives, and if they set a significant goal and dedicate themselves to it, they can achieve remarkable success.

Y.M. Sudha, Senior Civil Judge, spoke about how modern women should challenge societal inequalities and gender discrimination in today’s society. She encouraged women to take confident steps forward in life and act in ways that prevent violence against women. She urged women to be aware of the laws that protect them and to confidently take steps in society. She also advised women to live with patience and harmony, not wasting their potential, and to use their mobile phones responsibly and only when necessary. She emphasized that women should face life’s challenges with a harmonious attitude and prove that they can achieve anything.

Dr. G. Prasoon acted as the convener of the event. The college’s female staff members organized various cultural activities. The event saw participation from Dr. C. Subbarao, Director (AR&D); R.V. Ramana Murthy, Administrative Manager; various department heads; female teaching and non-teaching staff; and students.

title.rendered: Conducted an awareness program on road safety

content.rendered:
St. Ann’s College of Engineering and Technology, Chirala, conducted an awareness program on road safety, as stated in a joint announcement by the college secretary, Vanama Ramakrishna Rao, and correspondent, Srimantula Lakshmana Rao.

The college principal, Dr. K. Jagadish Babu, informed that the awareness program on road safety was organized under the guidance of the National Service Scheme (NSS) unit of the college. He mentioned that the chief guest for the event was Mohammad Moin, DSP, Chirala. Other attendees included Vetapalem Sub-Inspector M. Venkateswarlu and Chirala Circle Inspector P. Seshagiri Rao.

Speaking at the event, the principal, Dr. K. Jagadish Babu, emphasized that everyone traveling on the road should follow traffic rules and take necessary precautions to prevent accidents.

Vetapalem Sub-Inspector M. Venkateswarlu advised students against chasing vehicles while traveling on the road, highlighting that road dividers have been a cause of many deaths. Chirala Circle Inspector, P. Seshagiri Rao, stressed the importance of strictly following road safety rules and wearing helmets while riding two-wheelers. He pointed out the severe consequences of road accidents and warned against driving under the influence of alcohol.

The chief guest, Mohammad Moin, DSP, Chirala, urged all two-wheeler riders to wear helmets and ensure they possess a valid license. He stated that losing a family member in an accident brings immense grief and suffering to their loved ones. He also emphasized the importance of providing immediate medical assistance to accident victims. He mentioned that excessive bleeding in road accidents leads to many fatalities and that recovering from injuries can cost lakhs of rupees, pushing families into financial distress. He advised against using mobile phones while driving and encouraged students to study hard, secure good jobs, and make their parents and society proud.

During the event, the students honored the chief guest, Mohammad Moin, along with the CI and SI, by presenting them with shawls. The National Service Scheme (NSS) Coordinator, Dr. D. Jyothi Swaroop, served as the convener of the program. The event was attended by the college’s Administrative Manager, R.V. Ramanamurthy, Physical Education Instructor Annam Srinivasa Rao, various department heads, faculty members, and students.

title.rendered: 103 Students from St. Ann’s College of Engineering and Technology, Chirala, Selected for Sutherland Global Service

content.rendered:
The Secretary of St. Ann’s College of Engineering and Technology, Chirala, Mr. Vanama Ramakrishna Rao, and the Correspondent, Mr. Srimantula Lakshmana Rao, jointly announced that 103 students have been selected for the renowned Sutherland Global Services.

St. Ann’s College of Engineering and Technology, established in 2001 in Chirala, is recognized by the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), New Delhi, and permanently affiliated with Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University, Kakinada (JNTUK). Additionally, it holds an ‘A’ Grade from the Government of Andhra Pradesh and permanent recognition from the Institution of Engineers. The college has also been recognized as one of the top engineering colleges in India by surveys conducted by The Times of India and CEGR.

Dr. K. Jagadeesh Babu, Principal of the college, stated that 103 students from the 2025 graduating batch were selected through virtual campus placements conducted by Sutherland Global Services. The selected students include:

  • 31 from the CSE (Computer Science and Engineering) department,
  • 34 from the ECE (Electronics and Communication Engineering) department,
  • 4 from the EEE (Electrical and Electronics Engineering) department,
  • 5 from the Civil Engineering department,
  • 19 from the AI & ML (Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning) department,
  • 2 from the Cyber Security department,
  • 6 from the Data Science department,
  • 2 from the IoT (Internet of Things) department.

Mr. Nuthalapati Poornachandra Rao, Training and Placement Officer, mentioned that the selected students would receive an annual salary package of ₹2.70 lakhs along with other allowances.

The Director of Accreditations, Dr. C. Subbarao, Manager of Office Administration, Mr. R.V. Ramana Murthy, CSE Head Dr. P. Harini, ECE Head Dr. D. Rajendra Prasad, EEE Head Dr. K. Anil Kumar, Civil Engineering Head Mr. T. Kiran Kumar, AI & ML Head Dr. C. Hari Kishan, IoT Head Dr. S. Indranil, Cyber Security Head Dr. M. Ramesh, along with other heads of departments, faculty members, non-teaching staff, and students, congratulated the selected students on their achievement.

This was confirmed by Dr. Lakshmi Tulasi Chavali, Head of the Mechanical Engineering Department.

During his lecture, Dr. Prasad Patnaik B.S.V explained that the human heart functions like a double pump, and its design is deeply rooted in mechanical engineering principles. He elaborated on how the replacement of such a system could cost up to one crore rupees. He also emphasized that the human heart incorporates mechanical valve designs and pump mechanisms.

Dr. Prasad Patnaik B.S.V provided valuable insights into Modeling of Mechanical Circulatory Support Systems for the Human Body. He highlighted the increasing demand for biomedical equipment, innovative designs, and trained professionals in the biomedical engineering sector in India.

The guest lecture was attended by faculty members of the Mechanical Engineering Department and B.Tech second and third-year students, who actively participated and gained valuable knowledge from the session.

title.rendered: St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology Ranked among top 4th Institutions in Andhra Pradesh by IIRF 2023

content.rendered:
St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology, a premier institution in Andhra Pradesh, has secured a remarkable feat by ranking among the top 100 institutions in India, according to the India Institutional Ranking Framework (IIRF) 2023. The IIRF is a prestigious ranking system that evaluates the quality and performance of higher education institutions in India based on various parameters such as teaching, research, industry income, placement, and perception.

St. Ann’s College has achieved the 93rd rank at the national level, the 53rd rank of the Zone level, and the 4th rank at the state level in the IIRF 2023. This is a significant improvement from the previous year, when the college ranked 105th at the national level, 59th of the Zone level, and 5th at the state level. The college has also outperformed many other reputed institutions in its category and region.


The ranking is based on 7 performance indicators, deliberately focused on Indian socio economic and industrial scale varies across Placement Performance, Teaching Learning and Resources, Research, Industry Income and Integration, Placement Strategies and Support, and External Perception trusted nationwide by students, teachers, industry experts, and alumnus. The ranking reflects the excellence and commitment of St. Ann’s College in imparting quality education and fostering a culture of innovation and research among its students and faculty. The college has also been recognized for its social responsibility and contribution to the development of the society and the nation.

The prestigious IIRF award ceremony will take place on October 18, 2023 at The Ashok Chanakyapuri, New Delhi. This is a great honor for our college, as our Principal, Dr.M.VenuGopalaRao, will receive the award of top engineering college in India (private) from the IIRF. We are delighted to have the AICTE chairman, Prof. T.G.Sitaram, as the chief guest of the function. He will also deliver the keynote address and share his insights on the future of engineering education in India.


The college management, led by the Secretary Mr.Vanama Rama KrishanRao and Correspondent Mr.S.LakshmanaRao, have congratulated the principal, staff, and students for this remarkable achievement and expressed their gratitude to the parents, alumni, industry partners, and other stakeholders for their constant support and encouragement. The college has also thanked the IIRF team for their rigorous and transparent evaluation process and for acknowledging the efforts and achievements of St. Ann’s College. The college has vowed to continue its pursuit of excellence and innovation in engineering education and research and to strive for higher rankings in the future.

The Institution is approved by the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), New Delhi and is Permanently Affiliated to the Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University, Kakinada. The Institute offers 9 programs for Bachelor of Technology (B.Tech) – CIVIL, EEE, ME, ECE, CSE, IoT, AI&ML, DS & CS, 5 programs for Master of Technology (M.Tech), Master of Business Administration (MBA) and Master of Computer Application (MCA). Five Programmes were accredited 3 times by the National Board of Accreditation (NBA). The Institution is accredited 2 times by NAAC with an ‘A’ Grade. The Institution is recognized by UGC under sections 2(f) and 12(B). The Institution is awarded an ‘A’ grade by Andhra Pradesh State Government. The Institution is permanently accredited by the Institution of Engineers (I). The institute is ranked as one of the topmost engineering institutes across the country by various survey agencies, notably: Times of India and CEGR. The institute has State-of-the-art computer laboratories with high-end 1500 terminals, 200 Mbps (1:1) leased line internet connectivity, 200+ Faculty and 1/3 of them PhD holders and 100 either PhD Pursuing or M.Tech Holders, drawn from IITS & NITs. The institute faculty received Best Teacher & Best Researcher Awards from the University. The college consistently produces good results with an increased number of university ranks including Gold Medals. The institution stands State 4th in Pratibha Awards. 38 girl students got with 2 Lakhs Scholarship from AICTE in 2021. Centre for CIGS (Centre for GNSS ISRO studies) is established in the college in the year 2016 and it is involved in the design and development of space-borne instruments for ISRO missions and development and operationalization of applications of space technology for national development. SIEMENs Centre of Excellence for Technical Skill Development Institute (TSDI) was established in 2016 in collaboration with Andhra Pradesh state skill Development Corporation. This centre is having 6 laboratories with world-class industry -standard equipment worth Rs 2.5 corers. The institute has an IRM Centre (Infrastructure Rental Module) 550 High- End Systems, 160KV Generator. III years internships for students of close to 300 internships, some of them getting 15K/20K per month and the institute has decent standing of 500 ranking in the entire country and 150 in the southern region.
